bounded_question: What does function 0x514e160 do with its one string-view argument, and how does the global table at 0x578af60 decide the returned pointer?

callee.description: String-assign helper called with (destination string at rsp + 0x30, view struct at rsp + 0x10, flag 0). With flag 0 it takes the plain-assign arm: the destination becomes exactly the stripped view contents (pointer and stripped length from the struct). Its flag-nonzero arm is a per-byte nibble expansion and is NOT taken by this call; the nibble mapper it uses there is recorded separately.
callee.plain_assign_arm: calls the _M_replace PLT stub with (position 0, count 0, source pointer, source length) taken from the view struct
callee.temporary_disposal: after lookup, the temporary string is disposed by the standard rule: when its data pointer differs from its own SSO buffer address (rsp + 0x40), the sized-delete PLT stub is called with (pointer, capacity + 1); an SSO temporary deletes nothing

caller_sample.description: One enclosing caller function, cited as a consumer only; its wider semantics are not claimed. It passes its own third argument (a view pointer) as the window's argument.

censuses.note: Direct-call census by a full .text rel32 scan; tail-jump census by a full .text rel32 scan for the e9 opcode; qword census by a whole-file 8-byte-aligned scan. Callers are consumers only; no claim is made about their wider semantics, and the reaching path beyond them is not claimed.

hash_vectors.note: MurmurHash64A vectors for the library hash with seed 0xc70f6907, cross-checked against the VM's own libstdc++ _Hash_bytes (g++ build, same seed). The target binary calls the hash through a PLT stub, so these vectors validate the model hash implementation against the library algorithm, not by executing the target binary.

nibble_helper.description: Maps one nibble value 0..15 to its lowercase hexadecimal character: values 0..9 map to 0x30 + value, values 10..15 map to 0x37 + value. Used only by the callee's flag-nonzero arm, not by the window's call.

strip.description: Trailing ASCII decimal digits are removed from the view before lookup. Scanning from the last byte, each byte b with (b - 0x30) <= 9 unsigned is a digit; the scan stops at the first non-digit or when every byte has been consumed. The stripped length is the original length minus the trailing digit count, so an all-digit view strips to length 0 and an empty view stays empty.

hash_path.description: Compute the library hash of the stripped bytes with seed 0xc70f6907, take bucket = hash % bucket_count, and dereference the bucket slot once to reach the first node. Walk the chain following each node's +0x00 link. Before examining any node after the first, the walk checks that node's cached hash falls in the same bucket (cached hash % bucket_count == bucket); a node failing that check ends the chain with 0, as does a null link. A node matches when its cached hash at +0x70 equals the computed hash and its key length at +0x10 equals the stripped length and, for a nonzero length, its key bytes at +0x08 compare equal over that length (an empty search matches only a node whose key length is 0). The first match returns node + 0x28.

linear_path.description: Walk the global list starting at the node at +0x10, following each node's +0x00 link. A node matches when its key length at +0x10 equals the stripped length and, for a nonzero length, the key bytes at +0x08 compare equal over that length (an empty search matches only a node whose key length is 0, with no byte comparison). The first match returns node + 0x28; exhausting the list returns 0.

table.path_threshold: when the size at +0x18 is greater than 20 (unsigned), the hash-bucket path is used; otherwise the linear path is used

unknowns: The semantics of the payload at node + 0x28 and of the table's contents: the model returns the payload as an opaque value and does not interpret it.
How the table at 0x578af60 is populated, and what the keys denote: not observable from this window.
The reason for the size threshold of 20: recorded only as the observed branch condition.

The bucket slot's predecessor-link reading: the code dereferences the bucket slot once to reach the first node; the packet records that dereference as observed without naming the container's implementation.

The hash algorithm beyond the PLT symbol: the model implements the published libstdc++ _Hash_bytes algorithm (MurmurHash64A) and its vectors were cross-checked against the VM's libstdc++, not against an execution of the target binary.

window.arguments: rdi = pointer to a string view struct: byte pointer at +0x0, unsigned length at +0x8
window.canary: fs:0x28 stored at rsp + 0x58 and checked before return; mismatch calls the __stack_chk_fail PLT stub
window.returns: pointer to the matched node's payload at node + 0x28, or 0 when no node matches
